name: React
purpose: Component model with a virtual DOM; the default hiring pool. Now leans on Server Components and the compiler rather than manual memoisation

name: Angular
purpose: Batteries-included SPA framework — DI container, router, forms, HTTP client all first-party. Signals-based reactivity has largely replaced zone.js change detection

name: Vue
purpose: Component model with a compiler-optimised reactivity system; gentler ramp than React, strong first-party router/store

name: Svelte
purpose: Compiler, not a runtime — components compile to direct DOM updates. Runes give explicit, fine-grained reactivity

name: Solid
purpose: Fine-grained signals with no virtual DOM; ~10% adoption but the highest satisfaction score five years running in State of JS

name: Preact
purpose: 3KB React-API-compatible alternative; used where bundle size is the constraint (embeds, widgets)

name: Lit
purpose: Web Components with a thin reactive base class; framework-agnostic design systems

name: Qwik
purpose: Resumability instead of hydration — ships almost no JS until interaction

name: HTMX / Alpine.js
purpose: Hypermedia approach: server returns HTML fragments, tiny client library wires up interactions. The "no build step" counter-movement — popular with Rails/Django/Laravel/Go teams

name: jQuery
purpose: DOM manipulation and AJAX shim from the pre-framework era. Not a choice for new work, but 23.4% of developers still touch it

name: Next.js
purpose: The dominant full-stack React framework: App Router, Server Components, server actions, edge/node runtimes

name: Astro
purpose: Content-first, ships zero JS by default, "islands" for interactivity. Highest satisfaction in the category — 39 points above Next.js

name: Nuxt
purpose: Vue's equivalent of Next.js: file routing, SSR/SSG, auto-imports, large module ecosystem

name: SvelteKit
purpose: Official Svelte app framework — routing, form actions, adapters per host

name: React Router (v7/v8)
purpose: Absorbed Remix v2's loaders/actions; now both the React router and a full framework mode. v8 (June 2026) is ESM-only, yearly majors. Remix v2 and React Router v6 are end-of-life

name: Remix v3
purpose: Diverged: a zero-dependency full-stack framework that no longer uses React. Experimental — do not confuse with Remix v2

name: TanStack Start
purpose: Type-safe full-stack framework built on TanStack Router; the most-mentioned write-in in State of JS 2025

name: Angular SSR / Analog
purpose: Server rendering and hydration for Angular apps

name: Qwik City
purpose: Routing/SSR layer for Qwik

name: React Router
purpose: The de facto standard; nested routes, loaders, actions

name: TanStack Router
purpose: Fully type-safe routes and search-param parsing

name: Vue Router
purpose: Official router, nested + named views, navigation guards

name: Angular Router
purpose: Built in; guards, resolvers, lazy-loaded route modules

name: SvelteKit routing
purpose: Filesystem-based, part of the framework

name: TanStack Query (React Query, and Vue/Svelte/Solid ports)
purpose: Caching, deduplication, background refetch, stale-while-revalidate, optimistic updates. Removes the majority of what people used to write Redux for

name: SWR
purpose: Lighter stale-while-revalidate hook from the Next.js team

name: Apollo Client / urql
purpose: GraphQL clients with normalised caching

name: RTK Query
purpose: Data fetching bundled into Redux Toolkit

name: Zustand
purpose: Minimal store, hook-based
curated_signal: Now leads the category in both usage and satisfaction, having passed Redux (State of React 2025); ~44.5M downloads/week

name: Redux Toolkit
purpose: Single store, reducers, devtools, time-travel
curated_signal: Still the enterprise default for large, audit-heavy apps; ~35.8M/week for redux

name: Jotai
purpose: Atomic — bottom-up primitive atoms

name: Valtio / MobX
purpose: Proxy-based observable objects

name: XState
purpose: Statecharts / finite state machines
curated_signal: For genuinely complex flows: wizards, media players, checkout

name: Pinia
purpose: Vue's official store

name: NgRx / Angular signals
purpose: Redux pattern for Angular / built-in reactivity

name: Nano Stores / TanStack Store
purpose: Framework-agnostic tiny stores
curated_signal: Used in Astro islands and cross-framework design systems

name: Zod
purpose: TypeScript-first schema declaration and runtime validation; infers static types from schemas. Enormous reach — ~224M npm downloads/week, largely as a transitive dependency across the ecosystem

name: Valibot
purpose: Same idea, modular and far smaller bundle

name: React Hook Form
purpose: Uncontrolled-input form state with minimal re-renders; pairs with Zod via resolvers

name: TanStack Form
purpose: Type-safe, framework-agnostic form state

name: Formik
purpose: Older controlled-form library, largely superseded

name: VeeValidate
purpose: Validation for Vue forms

name: Angular Reactive Forms
purpose: Built-in typed form model

name: Tailwind CSS
purpose: Utility-first CSS; styling co-located with markup, no naming overhead. ~85.4M downloads/week

name: CSS Modules
purpose: Scoped class names, zero runtime — the boring safe default

name: Vanilla Extract / Panda CSS
purpose: Type-safe CSS authored in TS, compiled to static CSS at build time

name: styled-components / Emotion
purpose: CSS-in-JS. Declining — runtime cost conflicts with Server Components

name: shadcn/ui
purpose: Not a dependency: copy-in Radix + Tailwind components you own and edit

name: Radix UI / React Aria / Headless UI
purpose: Unstyled, accessible behaviour primitives (dialogs, comboboxes, menus) — the accessibility hard parts, no visual opinion

name: MUI / Ant Design / Chakra
purpose: Full opinionated design systems; fastest to a coherent-looking internal tool

name: PrimeNG / PrimeVue / Angular Material / Vuetify
purpose: Framework-specific component suites

name: Vite
purpose: Dev server (native ESM, instant HMR) + production bundler. Effectively the ecosystem standard
curated_signal: 84.4% usage, 98% satisfaction — the highest-rated tool in State of JS 2025; ~142.9M downloads/week

name: Rolldown / Rspack / esbuild / SWC
purpose: Rust- and Go-based bundlers/transpilers used underneath the tools above

name: Turbopack
purpose: Next.js's bundler

name: webpack
purpose: The former default; still everywhere in legacy config, but sentiment is clearly negative now

name: Turborepo / Nx
purpose: Monorepo task orchestration and caching

name: pnpm / npm / Bun / Yarn
purpose: Package management; pnpm's content-addressed store is the monorepo favourite

name: Biome / ESLint / Oxlint / Prettier
purpose: Linting and formatting; the Rust-based tools are displacing ESLint+Prettier on speed

name: Vitest
purpose: Vite-native unit/component test runner
curated_signal: 97% satisfaction, +14pts usage YoY; ~77.6M/week — closing fast on Jest

name: Jest
purpose: The incumbent unit test runner
curated_signal: Still #1 at 74.4% usage, but satisfaction is falling; ~39.5M/week

name: Playwright
purpose: Cross-browser end-to-end automation
curated_signal: 94% satisfaction, +14pts YoY — the clear E2E winner

name: Cypress
purpose: E2E with an interactive runner

name: Testing Library
purpose: Query DOM the way a user would; discourages testing implementation details

name: Storybook
purpose: Component workbench, visual review, interaction tests

name: MSW
purpose: Network-level API mocking shared across unit, component and E2E tests

name: Bun test / node:test / deno test
purpose: Runtime-bundled test runners — the emerging "no test framework" trend

name: React Native
purpose: Native iOS/Android from React; shares the web hiring pool. New Architecture (Fabric/TurboModules) is now default
curated_signal: ~10.4M npm downloads/week; present in 1,350 of the top 10k iOS apps, and in 173 apps earning $1M+/month vs Flutter's 37

name: Expo
purpose: The managed toolchain most React Native teams actually use: builds, OTA updates, native modules, routing

name: Flutter
purpose: Own rendering engine — pixel-identical across platforms, mobile/web/desktop
curated_signal: 177.9k GitHub stars; 11.07% of new App Store releases vs React Native's 6.75%

name: SwiftUI / Jetpack Compose
purpose: First-party declarative native UI. Best platform fidelity, two codebases

name: Kotlin Multiplatform + Compose Multiplatform
purpose: Share business logic (and increasingly UI) across Android/iOS/desktop

name: .NET MAUI
purpose: Cross-platform native UI for .NET shops

name: Electron
purpose: Desktop apps in Chromium + Node (VS Code, Slack)

name: Tauri
purpose: Same idea with the OS webview and a Rust core — far smaller binaries

name: NGINX
purpose: Reverse proxy, load balancer, TLS termination, static serving — the default ingress for two decades

name: Envoy
purpose: L7 proxy designed for dynamic service discovery, retries, circuit breaking, deep observability; the data plane under most meshes and modern gateways

name: Kong
purpose: API gateway on NGINX/Envoy: auth, rate limiting, quotas, key management, plugin ecosystem

name: Traefik
purpose: Cloud-native reverse proxy with automatic service discovery from Kubernetes/Docker labels

name: HAProxy
purpose: High-performance L4/L7 load balancing

name: Caddy
purpose: Reverse proxy with automatic HTTPS certificate management

name: Apache APISIX / Tyk / KrakenD
purpose: Alternative API gateways — APISIX is etcd-driven and hot-reloadable, KrakenD is stateless and aggregation-focused

name: AWS API Gateway / Azure API Management / Google Apigee
purpose: Managed equivalents with billing, developer portals, usage plans

name: Kubernetes Gateway API
purpose: The successor spec to Ingress; implemented by Envoy Gateway, Istio, Cilium, Kong, Traefik

name: Istio
purpose: The most feature-complete mesh. Ambient mode removes the per-pod sidecar, cutting the resource overhead that drove earlier complaints

name: Linkerd
purpose: Deliberately minimal, Rust micro-proxy, low overhead, fast to operate

name: Cilium / Cilium Service Mesh
purpose: eBPF-based networking, security policy and observability at the kernel level — no sidecar at all

name: Consul
purpose: Service discovery + mesh, strong outside Kubernetes and in mixed VM estates

name: Apache Kafka
purpose: Durable, replayable, partitioned event log. The backbone for event sourcing, CDC and stream processing

name: RabbitMQ
purpose: Traditional broker: queues, routing/exchange topologies, per-message ack. Best for task distribution and RPC-ish work

name: NATS / NATS JetStream
purpose: Extremely lightweight pub/sub with optional persistence; low-latency, edge and IoT friendly

name: Apache Pulsar
purpose: Segmented storage, multi-tenancy, geo-replication; separates compute from storage

name: Apache ActiveMQ / IBM MQ
purpose: JMS-era enterprise brokers, still ~6% each — heavily present in banking and insurance

name: AWS SQS/SNS/EventBridge, Azure Service Bus, Google Pub/Sub
purpose: Managed equivalents; the default when you're already all-in on a cloud

name: Redis Streams
purpose: Lightweight streaming when Redis is already in the stack

name: Apache Flink / Kafka Streams / Spark Structured Streaming
purpose: Stream processing — windowing, joins, stateful aggregation over those event logs

name: Debezium
purpose: Change-data-capture: turns database commits into Kafka events

name: Node/Express, Koa, Fastify (hooks), Hono
purpose: Body parsing, CORS, sessions, logging, rate limiting

name: ASP.NET Core
purpose: Auth, HTTPS redirect, exception handling, response compression

name: Django
purpose: Sessions, CSRF, auth, locale, security headers

name: Spring
purpose: Security chain, tracing, request logging

name: Go
purpose: Chi and Echo build their entire feature set from this

name: Rust/Tower
purpose: Timeouts, retries, concurrency limits — shared by Axum, Tonic and Hyper

name: REST + OpenAPI
purpose: Resource-oriented HTTP with a machine-readable contract that generates clients, docs and mocks

name: GraphQL (Apollo Server, GraphQL Yoga, Hot Chocolate, graphql-java, Strawberry)
purpose: Client specifies exactly what it needs; one endpoint, typed schema

name: gRPC + Protocol Buffers
purpose: Binary, HTTP/2, streaming, codegen in every language

name: tRPC
purpose: End-to-end TypeScript types with no codegen or schema

name: AsyncAPI
purpose: The OpenAPI equivalent for event-driven/message contracts

name: Webhooks / CloudEvents
purpose: Push notification of events between systems; CloudEvents standardises the envelope

name: Redis / Valkey
purpose: In-memory cache, session store, rate limiter, queue, pub/sub, distributed locks
curated_signal: 28% of all developers (SO 2025). Valkey is the Linux Foundation fork after Redis's licence change

name: Memcached
purpose: Pure, simple key-value cache

name: Varnish / CDN edge caches
purpose: HTTP-layer caching in front of the app

name: Elasticsearch / OpenSearch
purpose: Full-text search, log aggregation, analytics

name: Meilisearch / Typesense
purpose: Lightweight, fast, typo-tolerant search

name: pgvector / Qdrant / Weaviate / Milvus
purpose: Vector similarity search for embeddings and RAG

name: Keycloak
purpose: Self-hosted OIDC/SAML identity provider, federation, SSO

name: Auth0 / Okta / Microsoft Entra ID / AWS Cognito
purpose: Managed identity providers

name: Ory (Kratos/Hydra/Keto)
purpose: Composable, API-first identity, OAuth2 server and permissions

name: Auth.js (NextAuth) / Better Auth / Lucia
purpose: Application-level auth for JS/TS apps

name: Spring Security / ASP.NET Core Identity / Devise / Django auth
purpose: Framework-native auth and authorisation

name: Open Policy Agent (OPA) / Cedar / OpenFGA / SpiceDB
purpose: Externalised authorisation — policy as code, relationship-based access control

name: HashiCorp Vault / cloud secret managers
purpose: Secret storage, dynamic credentials, encryption as a service

name: Temporal
purpose: Durable execution — long-running, failure-tolerant workflows written as ordinary code

name: Apache Airflow / Dagster / Prefect
purpose: Scheduled data pipeline orchestration (DAGs)

name: Camunda / Zeebe
purpose: BPMN business process orchestration with human tasks

name: AWS Step Functions / Azure Durable Functions
purpose: Managed state-machine orchestration

name: Apache Camel / Spring Integration / MuleSoft
purpose: Classic enterprise integration patterns — routing, transformation, adapters to legacy systems

name: OpenTelemetry
purpose: Vendor-neutral standard for traces, metrics and logs. The only real answer to "how do I not get locked in?"

name: Prometheus + Grafana
purpose: Metrics collection, alerting, dashboards

name: Jaeger / Tempo / Zipkin
purpose: Distributed trace storage and query

name: Loki / ELK stack
purpose: Log aggregation

name: Sentry
purpose: Error tracking and performance monitoring, front and back end

name: Datadog / New Relic / Honeycomb
purpose: Commercial full-stack observability

name: Express
purpose: Minimal, unopinionated HTTP framework; the lingua franca of Node middleware

name: Fastify
purpose: Schema-driven, JSON-schema-validated, notably faster than Express with a plugin/encapsulation model

name: Hono
purpose: Ultralight, Web-Standards-based router that runs on Node, Bun, Deno, Cloudflare Workers, Lambda
curated_signal: S-tier satisfaction (>90%) in State of JS 2025; ~49.3M/week — an enormous rise

name: NestJS
purpose: Angular-style architecture for Node: DI, modules, decorators, guards, interceptors. The pick when a large team needs enforced structure

name: Koa
purpose: Express's successor from the same authors; async middleware, tiny core

name: Elysia
purpose: Bun-first framework with end-to-end type inference

name: FastAPI
purpose: Async, type-hint-driven API framework; validation and OpenAPI docs generated from Pydantic models. Now the most-used Python web framework

name: Flask
purpose: Microframework — routing and templating, everything else your choice

name: Django REST Framework
purpose: Serialisers, viewsets, auth and permissions on top of Django (20% usage)

name: Litestar
purpose: Modern async alternative to FastAPI with more built-in structure

name: Starlette
purpose: The ASGI toolkit underneath FastAPI (8%)

name: Uvicorn / Gunicorn
purpose: ASGI/WSGI servers that actually run the app

name: Spring Boot
purpose: Auto-configured, convention-over-configuration Spring. Ubiquitous in enterprise (14.7% of all developers in SO 2025); Spring Boot 4 / Framework 7 landed Nov 2025

name: Spring ecosystem
purpose: Spring MVC / WebFlux (blocking vs reactive web), Spring Data (repositories), Spring Security (authn/authz), Spring Cloud (config, discovery, resilience), Spring AI (LLM integration), Spring Batch

name: Quarkus
purpose: Kubernetes-native, build-time optimised, excellent GraalVM native-image support — fast startup, low memory

name: Micronaut
purpose: Compile-time DI and AOP (no runtime reflection); similar cold-start benefits

name: Helidon
purpose: Oracle's lightweight microservice framework; SE (reactive) and MP (MicroProfile) flavours

name: Jakarta EE 11
purpose: The vendor-neutral standard (Open Liberty, WildFly, Payara, GlassFish)

name: Vert.x
purpose: Event-driven, non-blocking toolkit for high-concurrency workloads

name: Ktor
purpose: Kotlin-first async framework, coroutine-based, DSL configuration

name: Micrometer
purpose: Metrics facade — the OpenTelemetry bridge for JVM apps

name: Minimal APIs
purpose: Low-ceremony endpoint definition for microservices

name: Blazor
purpose: C# in the browser via WebAssembly, or server-rendered over SignalR — frontend without JS (7.0%)

name: SignalR
purpose: Real-time bidirectional messaging (WebSockets with fallbacks)

name: Orleans
purpose: Virtual actor model for distributed stateful services

name: MassTransit / NServiceBus
purpose: Service-bus abstractions over RabbitMQ/Azure Service Bus — sagas, retries, outbox

name: ASP.NET (Framework)
purpose: The legacy .NET Framework stack, still at 14.2%

name: net/http (stdlib)
purpose: Now capable enough (method+path routing) that many teams skip frameworks entirely

name: Gin
purpose: Fast HTTP router + middleware, huge ecosystem — the most recommended option

name: Echo
purpose: Similar scope, cleaner API, built-in middleware set

name: Chi
purpose: Idiomatic: 100% compatible with net/http handler signatures, composable routers

name: Fiber
purpose: Express-like API on fasthttp; fastest benchmarks, deviates from stdlib interfaces

name: gRPC-Go / Connect
purpose: Service-to-service RPC; Connect speaks gRPC and plain HTTP

name: Axum
purpose: Ergonomic web framework built on Tokio/Tower/Hyper; composable middleware via Tower Layers. The current default

name: Actix Web
purpose: Actor-influenced, consistently at the top of throughput benchmarks

name: Rocket
purpose: Ergonomics-first with heavy macro use

name: Tokio
purpose: The async runtime everything else sits on

name: Tower
purpose: Reusable middleware abstraction (Service/Layer) shared across the ecosystem

name: Tonic
purpose: gRPC implementation on Tokio

name: SQLx
purpose: Async SQL with compile-time-checked queries against a live schema

name: Diesel / SeaORM
purpose: Full ORMs — Diesel is sync and type-safe, SeaORM is async

name: Serde
purpose: Serialisation/deserialisation — near-universal

name: Leptos / Dioxus / Yew
purpose: Rust frontend frameworks compiling to WebAssembly

name: Laravel
purpose: Full-stack, developer-experience-focused: Eloquent ORM, queues, Blade templates, Livewire/Inertia for reactive UI without a separate SPA

name: Symfony
purpose: Component-based and standards-driven; the reusable components underpin Laravel, Drupal and others

name: WordPress
purpose: CMS, not a framework — but 13.6% of all developers work with it (SO 2025)

name: Slim / Laminas / CodeIgniter
purpose: Microframework and legacy-enterprise options

name: Doctrine
purpose: Data Mapper ORM (Symfony's default); Eloquent is the Active Record counterpart

name: Tooling
purpose: Composer (packages) · PHPUnit 50% · Pest 17% (rising) · PHPStan 36% (static analysis, rising fast) · Rector (automated refactoring)

name: Ruby on Rails
purpose: The original convention-over-configuration full-stack framework; Active Record, migrations, Action Cable. 5.9% (SO 2025)

name: Hotwire (Turbo + Stimulus)
purpose: Rails' answer to SPAs: server-rendered HTML over the wire, minimal JS

name: Sidekiq
purpose: Redis-backed background jobs — near-universal in Rails apps

name: Sinatra / Hanami / Roda
purpose: Lightweight and alternative-architecture frameworks

name: RSpec / Minitest
purpose: Testing

name: Phoenix
purpose: Fault-tolerant, massively concurrent web framework on the BEAM VM; 2.4% (SO 2025)

name: Phoenix LiveView
purpose: Real-time server-rendered UI over WebSockets with no client-side framework — the most mature version of this idea

name: Vapor
purpose: Server-side Swift

name: Play / Akka (Pekko)
purpose: Reactive web and actor-based concurrency

name: Deno Fresh
purpose: Islands architecture on Deno

name: Shiny / Plumber
purpose: Data-science web apps and APIs
